chunks: And from him, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayub, from Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Durays al-Kunasi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Do you know from where adultery entered among the people?" I said: "I do not know." He said: "From our khums, the Ahl al-Bayt, except for our pure Shias, for it is permissible for them and for their offspring."

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: Why did adultery enter the people according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the consumption of khums by the Ahl al-Bayt as the root cause of zina entering the general community, distinguishing this from the pure Shia (al-Shi'ah al-Aṭyabīn) for whom it remains halal. This hadith highlights the theological principle that the spiritual state of the community is linked to the purity and usage of the Imams' wealth, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the distribution of khums.
